summary: Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist. He served as Professor of Samskrta at Gujarat Vidyapith and L. D. Arts College (attested 1938), and as Professor of Sanskrit at S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women.

Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar earned an M.A. from the University of Mumbai and a doctorate from the University of Heidelberg. He was a professor at Fergusson College and Savitribai Phule Pune University, and served as Honorary Secretary of BORI (1939–2001).

Historian and Indologist Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was educated at Presidency College, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as professor and vice-chancellor at the University of Dhaka (1921–1942) and held principalships at Banaras Hindu University and RTM Nagpur University.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte was an Indologist and historian. In 1967, he served as Head of the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and held visiting lectureships at Wake Forest, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State.

Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
Ramkrishna Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Calcutta. He served on the faculty at Ananda Mohan College from approximately 1974 to 2007.
Ramon Prats is a Tibetologist. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who was taught by Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral studies under Richard K. Payne.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at UC Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as a professor at the City University of Hong Kong (c. 1996–2007) and took up a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai (2021).

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied traditionally under Attaragama Gnanawimala and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and trained numerous students such as Chögyam Trungpa and Pema Chödrön.
Raniero Gnoli was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at the University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested in 2003 and 2017).
Raphael Kühner was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (c. 1821–1825). His students included Georg Bühler.

Raphael von Koeber was a philosopher who studied at the Moscow Conservatory, the University of Jena, and the University of Heidelberg. He held an appointment at the University of Tokyo beginning in 1893.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College under R. D. Ranade, and later under Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinavijaya. He served as Professor of Samskrta and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (c. 1920–1930).

Rasmus Rask was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies educated at the University of Copenhagen. He founded the Royal Society of Northern Antiquaries and held multiple posts at Copenhagen, including professor of Eastern languages (1831).
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and succeeded him in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Boise State and Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary, and was appointed Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State (~2013).

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Lucknow, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute, and Kumaun. He worked in Haryana's archaeology department, taught at the Institute of Archaeology, New Delhi, and became Director General of the ASI.
